title: First DARCYS Awards Honor Disability Stories in Film and TV
summary:
On Saturday, Easterseals held the first Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards—nicknamed The DARCYs—in Santa Monica, California. The ceremony, formerly known as the Media Access Awards, celebrates authentic disability representation in movies, television, and media.

Among the inaugural winners highlighted in coverage were the HBO Max drama "The Pitt" and the Sundance film "Take Me Home." In the published winners list, "Horsegirls" took Best Feature, Anna Sargent won recognition tied to "Take Me Home," and "The Haunting of Pennhurst" won Best Documentary. Committees of filmmakers, critics, past honorees, and guild and nonprofit representatives chose nominees and winners; most committee members are people with disabilities.

Comedian and disability advocate Tina Frim hosted. The night also honored Geri Jewell with the inaugural DARCYS Legacy Award and Vincent Rutley with the Christopher Reeve Emerging Talent Award. Artist and disability culture leader Lachi performed. Easterseals Southern California and Film Independent co-produced the event at the Historic Barker Hangar.

Nancy Weintraub of Easterseals Southern California said the awards continue a legacy that began in 1979 and congratulate storytellers "changing how disability is seen." Shawn Davis of Film Independent called the DARCYS a new chapter in recognizing artists who broaden perspectives on screen and behind the scenes.

Guests included Marlee Matlin and other actors and advocates. For kids who love movies, the message is clear: inclusive casting and storytelling are being celebrated as part of excellence in entertainment.
why_it_matters: Awards spotlight stories that include disabled people honestly. Kids who love movies can see that inclusion is part of creative excellence.
